scope: mio reactor queued/in-flight active TCP registration liveness
root_cause: has_pending counted only live registrations; queued or dequeued-in-flight RegisterActive commands had no liveness ownership
fix: Registration-only RAII guards increment shared per-handle pending count before enqueue and survive dequeue/handling. Release after live registration publication or on failure/discard/receiver disconnect. Read handoff count before live count with Acquire; guard completion uses Release.

deterministic_tests.isolation: Separate test subprocess owns socket registry/global counters. No reactor thread runs. Lifecycle checkpoints are advanced manually; actual drain loop is observed after dequeue, before handler publication. One real loopback fd supplies successful poll registration, without peer data.
deterministic_tests.red: All three tests fail at intended queued/in-flight ownership assertions on original main, not setup/compile errors.
deterministic_tests.early_release_counter_verification: Temporarily drop the registration guard immediately after dequeue in the final processing loop; the success test fails at its in-flight assertion. Source restored in finally before final checks.
deterministic_tests.green: All three pass on final source; include registration reuse, live handoff/deregistration, missing socket, ordinary registration discard, cleanup without wake source, 100 failed sends, independent clone/command lifetimes, shutdown with queued registration.

native_focused.note: Earlier focused run; all tests also included in final full native suite.

limits: Local macOS arm64 only; no new Linux/Windows/runtime cross-platform verdict. Non-mio active-reader fallback unchanged.
Cowlib/EUnit suites not rerun for this internal reactor change; full native Erlang suite passed on final integration source. Two existing Onecached integration skips remain.
Existing relative TCP performance/stress regression passes, but no new before/after throughput or absolute latency measurement.
Only registration ownership is corrected; not a claim that all reactor/scheduler concurrency paths have been audited.
CI/Release remain manually suspended; no workflows enabled or changed.
